title: Vinted Sale Complete but Buyer Wants a Refund Weeks or Months Later — Do You Have to Pay?
intro: No — once a Vinted order is complete (the buyer pressed “Everything is OK” or the 2-day confirmation window passed without an issue being raised), the payment is yours and Vinted can no longer process a refund, return or compensation for that order. A buyer messaging you days, weeks or even months later to demand money back is asking for something Vinted itself no longer supports — and you're not a shop with a warranty. Here's exactly where you stand and how to handle it without getting bullied into paying.
meta_description: A Vinted buyer wants a refund after the sale is complete — weeks or months later. Do you have to pay? Your rights as a seller, the 2-day window, and how to handle threats and negative feedback.
author: Supervint Team
cta_text: Get alerted the moment genuine listings appear — and stop wasting time on problem buyers

body.heading: No — once the order is complete, you're not obliged to refund
paragraphs: This is one of the most repeated seller questions on r/vinted, r/vintedUK and the big Facebook Vinted seller groups: the order finished, the money landed in the wallet, and then the buyer comes back — a few days, a few weeks or a few months later — claiming the item is faulty, “see through”, the wrong size, or that it stopped working, and demanding a refund. Recent threads include a buyer complaining an LED light “stopped working” three months after delivery, a buyer demanding a refund three months after the sale was completed and turning to threats when the seller said it was too late, and a buyer who pressed “Everything is OK”, then changed her mind a few hours later.

Vinted's own help page for this exact situation — “The buyer has an issue, but the order is completed” — is unambiguous: “The order is now complete, and the payment has been released to your Vinted Wallet. This means we can no longer offer a refund, compensation, or a return for the order.” The order either completed because the buyer pressed “Everything is OK”, or because they didn't report anything in time and it auto-completed — and Vinted states that “this action can't be reversed”. Once it's done, Buyer Protection ends with it.

So when a buyer messages you after completion demanding money back, the answer is no — calmly, once, in the Vinted chat. You're a private seller, not a retailer, and Vinted gives buyers no right to a refund outside that window.

body.heading: The 2-day confirmation window is the whole system
paragraphs: To understand why you're in the clear, you need to know how Vinted's order confirmation actually works. When a parcel is marked as delivered, the buyer gets a 2-day confirmation period. Vinted's help pages are consistent on this: “When we notify you that the package should have been delivered, you have 2 days to report an issue and submit a refund request.” During those 2 days the buyer must either press “Everything is OK” to release your payment, or press “I have an issue” to suspend the order and request a refund.

If they press neither, the order completes automatically when the period ends — and per Vinted's refund policy, “If you don't report any issues in time (or if you confirm you accept an order), your payment will be sent to the seller and we'll be unable to support you with a refund.” The policy is equally blunt about completed orders: “refunds are no longer possible”.

It's also worth knowing what isn't covered even inside the window: an item that “doesn't fit or doesn't suit you” is not eligible for a return or refund under Vinted's refund policy — it explicitly says the buyer can ask, but “it's their decision” whether the seller accepts. The same goes for items “used extensively or damaged after a successful delivery”. A buyer who wore something, used it for weeks or simply changed their mind has no leg to stand on — before or after completion.

body.heading: Why this keeps happening: buyer's remorse, “warranty” claims and refund fishing
paragraphs: The threads make the motives pretty clear. Some buyers genuinely believe second-hand purchases come with a warranty, like the seller whose buyer came back months later saying a light “doesn't work anymore” — when the item had worked fine at delivery and for weeks of use. Others have plain buyer's remorse: the sale completes, the dopamine wears off, and they want their money back because the item isn't as flattering or as exciting as they hoped. A few are deliberately pushing it — claiming a brand-new item was “heavily worn” after the order had already completed, or trying to guilt-trip sellers into a refund they know the platform won't give them.

Sellers in these threads consistently give each other the same advice: “You're not a shop and don't offer a warranty”, “not your problem”, “block and move on”. One seller's verdict on buyers treating private sellers like a store: “these people need to stop shopping online from private sellers and go back to brick and mortar stores”. Harsh, but it captures the legal reality: a private sale on Vinted carries no ongoing guarantee, and the 2-day reporting window exists precisely so problems are raised while the money can still be protected — not months down the line.

body.heading: What to do when a buyer messages you after the sale is done
paragraphs: First, reply once — politely, in the Vinted chat, never by phone or off-platform — and keep it short: the order is complete, the payment has been released, and the 2-day window for reporting issues has passed, so you're not able to offer a refund. You don't need to argue the merits of their claim, and you definitely shouldn't get drawn into a long back-and-forth; sellers who over-explain often regret it, and the thread advice is that one clear answer is plenty.

Don't accept an “off-Vinted” return either — sellers who tried report returns going to random lockers they couldn't collect from, leaving them out of pocket with no protection. If you do want to help (more below), keep everything in the app.

If the buyer keeps pushing, starts insulting you, or escalates to threats — one recent Facebook post describes a buyer who “demanded a refund and turned to threats”, called the seller a liar on sizing, and said it was “a good job they're forgiving” — stop replying and block them. Keep screenshots of anything abusive first. And don't be rattled if Vinted support's generic reply tells you to “sort it out with the buyer”: when no issue has been raised on the order, that's boilerplate — there is no open case, your money isn't held, and nothing will happen to it while you two talk in the chat.

body.heading: Negative feedback after a completed sale: your actual options
paragraphs: The one real headache is feedback. Buyers can leave feedback within 4 days of an order completing, so a disgruntled buyer can still hit you with a 1-star review after pressing “Everything is OK” — one seller in the threads was left a “disgraceful service” review for refusing a refund she wasn't entitled to. You can't delete feedback left for you yourself, but you do have options:

Reply to it. Vinted lets you respond to feedback you've received, and a calm, factual reply — “the sale was completed after the 2-day confirmation period; the buyer asked for a refund after completion, which Vinted's policy doesn't allow” — tells future buyers the real story. Anyone weighing that review will see both sides.

Ask the buyer to edit or remove it — once, politely, after things have cooled down. It sometimes works. And if the feedback crosses a line — harassment, threats, personal information, or anything else that breaks Vinted's community standards — report it. Vinted states it only removes automatic feedback or feedback that “violates our Community Standards or applicable laws”, and that accounts leaving such feedback “may be blocked”. A buyer's false complaint about a completed sale is not, on its own, grounds for removal — but threats and abuse are.

body.heading: When you genuinely should help — and when to stand firm
paragraphs: None of this means “never help anyone”. The line is simple: if a buyer raises a genuine issue inside the 2-day window — the item arrived significantly not as described, damaged, or missing — that's a real suspended order and you should engage with it properly in the app (photos, honest assessment, and a resolution: full refund, partial refund, or return). That's the system working as designed.

After the window closes, any refund is a voluntary goodwill gesture, not an obligation. Some sellers reasonably choose to help a buyer who spots a genuine fault within a day or two and made an honest mistake. But you're equally within your rights to decline a return demand that arrives weeks or months after completion — especially when the item was used in the meantime — and there's nothing Vinted will do to force you. Know the rules, give one clear answer, and don't let a persistent buyer turn a finished sale into a negotiation.

faq.question: A buyer wants a refund weeks or months after the sale completed — do I have to pay?
faq.answer: No. Once the order is complete (the buyer pressed “Everything is OK” or the 2-day confirmation window passed), the payment is released to you and Vinted's help page states it “can no longer offer a refund, compensation, or a return for the order”. A private sale carries no ongoing warranty — a late refund demand is not something you have to agree to.

faq.question: What is the 2-day confirmation period on Vinted?
faq.answer: It starts when the parcel is marked as delivered. The buyer has 2 calendar days to either press “Everything is OK” (releasing your payment) or press “I have an issue” (suspending the order and requesting a refund). If they do nothing, the order completes automatically — Vinted says this can't be reversed.

faq.question: The buyer says the item stopped working or broke after a few weeks — can they force a refund?
faq.answer: No. Vinted's refund policy says items “used extensively or damaged after a successful delivery” are not eligible for refunds or returns, and after completion refunds aren't possible at all. Items that fail after real use aren't covered by any warranty — you sold it as a private seller, not a shop.

faq.question: A buyer left me negative feedback after the completed sale — can I get it removed?
faq.answer: You can't delete feedback left for you, but you can reply to it with a calm factual explanation, and you can ask the buyer to edit or remove it. Vinted only removes automatic feedback or feedback that violates its Community Standards or laws — threats, harassment and personal data qualify — and accounts leaving such feedback may be blocked.

faq.question: Should I accept the return just to keep the buyer happy?
faq.answer: That's your choice, not your obligation. If you do, keep everything inside Vinted's chat and system — sellers who arranged returns off-platform report parcels sent to random lockers, leaving them out of pocket with no protection. After the confirmation window, any refund or return you accept is a goodwill gesture.

faq.question: The buyer is threatening me in messages — what can I do?
faq.answer: Stop engaging, block them, and screenshot the messages first. Threats and harassment break Vinted's community standards and are grounds for reporting the member — feedback and messages like that can get the account blocked. Give your one clear answer, then don't negotiate with someone who's turned to abuse.
